wikipedia#1.title: 2009: A crowd of people on their way to register Esmael Mangudadatu's candidacy for governor of Maguindanao, Philippines, were kidnapped and killed by supporters of his rival, resulting in 58 deaths.

wikipedia#2.title: 2007: MS Explorer became the first cruise ship to sink in the Southern Ocean.

wikipedia#3.title: 2003: Rose Revolution: Eduard Shevardnadze resigned as President of Georgia following weeks of mass protests over disputed election results.

wikipedia#4.title: 1996: Ethiopian Airlines Flight 961 was hijacked, then ran out of fuel and crashed into the Indian Ocean, killing 125 of the 175 people on board.

wikipedia#5.title: 1980: An earthquake struck the Irpinia region of Italy, killing at least 2,483 people, injuring more than 7,700 and leaving 250,000 homeless.

wikipedia#6.title: 1976: Jacques Mayol became the first person to freedive to a depth of 100 metres (330 ft).

wikipedia#7.title: 1963: The first episode of Doctor Who, the world's longest-running science fiction television show, was broadcast on BBC television, starring William Hartnell as the first incarnation of the title role.

wikipedia#8.title: 1924: The New York Times published evidence from Edwin Hubble (pictured) stating that the Andromeda Nebula, previously believed to be part of the Milky Way, is in fact another galaxy.

wikipedia#9.title: 1876: William "Boss" Tweed, a New York City politician who had been arrested for embezzlement, was handed over to US authorities after having escaped from prison and fled to Spain.

wikipedia#10.title: 1867: The Manchester Martyrs were hanged in Manchester, England, for involvement in a scheme to free two Irish nationalists from custody in which a police officer was killed.

wikipedia#11.title: 1733: African slaves in the Danish West Indies began an insurrection in one of the earliest and longest slave revolts in the Americas.

wikipedia#12.title: 1700: A papal conclave, which had been deadlocked due to concerns over how a successor would respond to the impending death of Charles II of Spain, ended with the election of Clement XI.

wikipedia#13.title: 1644: In opposition to licensing and censorship during the English Civil War, John Milton's Areopagitica was published, arguing for the right to free expression.

wikipedia#14.title: 1635: Dutch pacification campaign on Formosa: Soldiers from the Dutch East India Company (flag depicted) razed the village of Mattau, now part of modern-day Tainan, Taiwan.
